title: A lisse continuous sheaf has a lisse integral model on a nonempty reduced open
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]; noetherian means a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, and finite-dimensional means a finite bound on lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. Write $A_Y(V)=C(|V|,A)$ and $E_Y(V)=C(|V|,E)$ on the small pro-etale site of any locally closed subscheme $Y$ of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $S_Y(M)=E_Y\otimes_{A_Y}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Constructible integral means continuous-constructible as in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module], with local models $A_Y\otimes_A P$ for finitely presented $A$-modules $P$ on finitely many locally closed strata. Assume that $X$ is nonempty and reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Let $L$ be an $E_X$-module sheaf pro-etale locally free of finite rank, meaning a pro-etale covering makes it a finite direct sum of its coefficient sheaf; ranks may vary and may be zero. There is a nonempty quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and an $A_U$-module sheaf $M_U$ pro-etale locally free of finite rank such that $S_U(M_U)\cong j^{-1}L$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, first paragraph, followed by extraction of a nonempty open from its finite stratification; Stacks Tag 03S0 (etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-etale-stratified-finite).

proof.text: We will use restriction to open subschemes with the following explicit conventions. The localization equivalence identifies the small pro-etale site of an open $V\subset T$ with the slice at $V$. Its coefficient restriction has value $C(|Z|,A)$, respectively $C(|Z|,E)$, on $Z\to V$, hence is exactly $A_V$, respectively $E_V$. Restricting a trivializing cover gives a covering of $V$ and restricts $A_T^{\oplus r}$ to $A_V^{\oplus r}$ (likewise for $E$), so local finite freeness survives. The ringed-topos tensor comparison identifies the restriction of $E_T\otimes_{A_T}M$ with $E_V\otimes_{A_V}(M|_V)$. Thus an integral lattice pair restricts to an integral lattice pair on every open. These statements also apply to an open in a member of an etale covering, without any quasi-compactness assumption on that member.

source.place: Definition 6.8.1, Proposition 6.8.4(6); slice restriction and Stacks 03EL (sites-modules-lemma-tensor-product-pullback)

proof.text: Apply etale-local lattice existence to $L$. Obtain an etale covering family $(Y_i\to X)_i$ and lisse $A_{Y_i}$-modules $M_i$ with $E_{Y_i}\otimes_{A_{Y_i}}M_i\cong L|_{Y_i}$. Since $X$ is nonempty and the family is jointly surjective, some $Y_i$ has a point. Choose a nonempty affine open $B\subset Y_i$ and restrict this lattice pair to $B$ as in step 1. Put $M_B=M_i|_B$.

Let $W$ be the image of $B\to X$. It is nonempty and open because the etale map $Y_i\to X$ is open. The map $p:B\to W$ is etale and surjective: in the affine-local definition of etaleness, restricting the source or restricting the target to an open containing the entire image leaves the same local ring maps. The open subscheme $W$ is noetherian and therefore quasi-compact; it is quasi-separated by local noetherianity. The affine scheme $B$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These are the hypotheses needed to stratify $p$.

source.place: Tag 03S0 (lemma-etale-stratified-finite), hypotheses; properties.tex Tags 01OW, 01OY; morphisms.tex Tag 03WT

proof.text: Apply the finite-etale stratification theorem to $p:B\to W$. It gives a finite partition by locally closed subschemes $S_a\to W$ such that $B\times_W S_a\to S_a$ is finite etale. No lattice descent has been used yet.

Some stratum contains a nonempty open of $W$. Here is the finite topological argument. Set $C_a=\overline{|S_a|}$; these finitely many closed sets cover $W$. Choose a subfamily minimal among those covering $W$, and one index $a$ in it. Then $O=W\setminus\bigcup_{b\ne a}C_b$ (union over that subfamily) is nonempty, open, and contained in $C_a$. Since $S_a$ is locally closed, write $|S_a|=H_a\cap C_a$ with $H_a$ open. Density of $|S_a|$ in $C_a$ shows $U=O\cap H_a$ is nonempty. It is open in $W$, hence open in $X$, and its underlying set is contained in $|S_a|$.

source.place: Tag 03S0; elementary extraction of an open from a finite locally closed partition

proof.text: Regard $U$ as the open subscheme of $X$. It is reduced, since its local rings are those of the reduced scheme $X$. Factor the immersion $S_a\to W$ as a closed immersion $S_a\to T$ followed by an open immersion $T\to W$. Its set-theoretic image contains $U$, so $U\subset T$. The reduced-source factorization lemma applied to $U\to T$ gives a factorization $U\to S_a\to T$. Consequently $U$ maps to $S_a$ over $W$. This supplies the actual scheme morphism required to base change over $S_a$, rather than inferring factorization from containment of sets alone.

source.place: Tag 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction), applied to the closed part of the stratum immersion

proof.text: Put $B_U=B\times_W U$ and $p_U:B_U\to U$. Because $U\to W$ factors through $S_a$, $p_U$ is the base change of the finite etale map $B\times_W S_a\to S_a$; hence it is finite etale. It is surjective by base change of the single-member etale cover $p:B\to W$. The projection $B_U\to B$ identifies $B_U$ with the open inverse image of $U$. Restrict the pair $(M_B,E_B\otimes_{A_B}M_B\cong L|_B)$ to this open, using step 1. This supplies a lisse $A_{B_U}$-module with rationalization $p_U^{-1}(L|_U)$. Here every inverse image along an object $r:Z\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (for $Z=Y_i,B,B_U,U$) is identified with the slice restriction, $r^{-1}G\cong G|_Z$ naturally for sheaves of sets, abelian groups and rings, by the object inverse-image restriction lemma; applied to $E_X$, to $L$ and to the action map, and with $E_X|_Z=E_Z$ from step 1, this identifies $u_i^{-1}L$ restricted to $B_U$ with $L|_{B_U}$ as $E_{B_U}$-modules. The equality of the two restrictions of $L$, $L|_{B_U}\cong p_U^{-1}(j^{-1}L)$, uses the canonical inverse-image composition comparison for $B_U\to U\to X$, whose monoidality also preserves the scalar-extension identification.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, first paragraph; finite etale base change: Stacks 01WL, 02GO, 01S1; inverse-image composition and tensor comparison: 00X6, 03EL

proof.text: The open subscheme $U$ is noetherian and quasi-compact by noetherian-open permanence. Its underlying space is noetherian: take a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, apply the affine noetherian-space theorem to each chart, then the finite-union theorem to that cover. The restriction $L|_U$ is lisse by step 1. Thus finite-etale lattice descent applies to the finite etale surjection $p_U$ and the lattice of step 7. It yields a lisse $A_U$-module $M_U$ with $E_U\otimes_{A_U}M_U\cong L|_U\cong j^{-1}L$, the last isomorphism by the object inverse-image restriction lemma for the open immersion $j$ (an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$), compatible with the $E_U$-actions as in step 7. This is the required scalar-extension isomorphism. For every affine open $V\subset X$, first $V$ and then $U\cap V$ are noetherian by the same open permanence. Thus $j^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact: $j$ is a quasi-compact morphism as well. Nonemptiness was proved in step 5, and no step imposes positive or constant rank.
